ai_summary: Current system dynamics underscore Scotland’s critical contribution to renewable power alongside ongoing transmission constraints across Great Britain. Total GB wind output currently stands at 9.6 GW, anchored by an estimated Scottish wind output of 3.7 GW, which accounts for 36.6% of installed Scottish wind capacity. Driven by this clean generation volume, Scottish carbon intensity has dropped to 0 gCO2/kWh, presenting a stark regional contrast to the GB-wide carbon intensity of 115 gCO2/kWh. However, structural transmission limitations continue to restrict the transfer of zero-carbon power to demand centers further south. As a direct consequence, Scottish generation curtailed so far today has reached 17460.8 MWh, accumulating a constraint cost of about £641,287. Because this low-cost, zero-carbon electricity cannot reach consumers, alternative generation was fired up elsewhere on the network. This operational constraint resulted in an estimated 3317552.0 m3 of gas burned elsewhere to replace it, driving an avoidable 6111.3 tonnes CO2 into the atmosphere. These metrics illustrate the immediate operational reality facing the grid, where localized renewable abundance without sufficient export capacity creates substantial consumer costs and displaces zero-carbon generation with thermal alternatives.
